questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which kinds of deposits may a payments bank accept under RBI's Payments Banks – Miscellaneous Directions, 2025?

options.text: Savings, current and fixed deposits up to ₹2 lakh
Only fixed deposits of up to one year
Recurring deposits only
Only demand deposits, i.e. current and savings deposits

solution.explanation: Payments banks may undertake only restricted activities such as accepting demand deposits — current and savings bank deposits. They cannot accept term deposits, and the ₹2 lakh end-of-day cap per individual applies.
solution.why_others_wrong: Fixed and recurring deposits are term deposits, which payments banks cannot accept.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Only demand deposits, i.e. current and savings deposits

fact_checks.claim: PBs may undertake only certain restricted activities such as acceptance of demand deposits, i.e., current deposits, and savings bank deposits

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

options.text: Balance enquiry and account statement download
Funds transfer to another bank
Applying for and receiving a loan
Bill payments from the account

solution.explanation: A view-only facility offers only services that do not alter the customer's assets or liabilities, such as balance enquiry, balance viewing and statement download. Fund transfers and other facilities that move funds or create liability need a transactional facility.
steps: View only = no change in assets/liabilities
solution.why_others_wrong: Fund transfers, loans and bill payments move funds or create liabilities.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Balance enquiry and account statement download

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A company has fund-based and non-fund-based facilities of ₹12 crore from the banking system and wants a current account with a payments bank. Under the current account rules in RBI's Payments Banks – Miscellaneous Directions, 2025 (as updated), what can the payments bank offer?

options.text: A normal current account without restriction
Only a collection account, whose credits must be remitted within two working days to the designated cash credit, overdraft or current account
Nothing, as payments banks cannot open current accounts
A current account, provided the balance stays below ₹2 lakh

solution.explanation: A bank may maintain a current account without restriction only where the banking system's aggregate exposure to the customer is below ₹10 crore. At ₹10 crore or more, only a collection account is allowed; funds credited must be remitted within two working days to the designated CC/OD/current account (after statutory dues and dues to the bank). ₹12 crore ≥ ₹10 crore, so only a collection account.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹12 crore exceeds the threshold; payments banks can open current accounts; the ₹2 lakh cap concerns individuals.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Only a collection account, whose credits must be remitted within two working days to the designated cash credit, overdraft or current account

fact_checks.claim: A bank may maintain current account without any restriction in case of customers where the aggregate exposure of the banking system to the customer is less than ₹10 crore ... A bank may maintain only collection accounts in case of customers to whom the exposure of the banking system is ₹10 crore or more

Funds credited into a collection account shall be remitted within two working days of receipt of such funds to a Cash Credit Account (CC), current account, or Overdraft Account (OD) ... designated by the borrower

questions.question_text: On 10 November 2026 a payments bank finds that the banking system's exposure to a customer holding an ordinary current account with it has risen to ₹10.5 crore. Under RBI's Payments Banks – Miscellaneous Directions, 2025, what must it do?

options.text: Close the account the same day
Nothing until the next half-yearly review
Convert the account into a savings account within a week
Notify the customer by 10 December 2026 that the account must be converted to a collection account or closed, and complete this by 10 February 2027

solution.explanation: Banks must monitor accounts at least once every half-year. When a customer becomes ineligible because exposure has reached ₹10 crore, the bank must notify the customer promptly and within one month that the account must be converted to a collection account or closed, and complete the conversion or closure within three months of observing the ineligibility.
solution.why_others_wrong: Immediate closure is not required; waiting for the review or converting to savings is not the rule.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Notify the customer by 10 December 2026 that the account must be converted to a collection account or closed, and complete this by 10 February 2027

fact_checks.claim: the bank shall notify the customer(s) concerned promptly, and in any case within one month from the date of observing such ineligibility, that the account must either be converted to a collection account or closed. Voting rights are capped at 10%, and acquiring 1% needs RBI's approval
There is no cap on voting rights for SFBs
Acquisition of up to 25% needs no approval

solution.concept: Voting rights in private banks and SFBs

options.text: On RBI's reference rate for gold on the redemption day
On the simple average of the closing price of 999-purity gold for the previous three business days, as published by the India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA)
On the issue price plus accrued interest
On the London Bullion Market price converted at the RBI reference rate

All successful bids are accepted at a single cut-off price
Prices are fixed in advance by RBI
Only non-competitive bids are accepted

questions.question_text: RBI's money market data for 5 November 2026 show overnight volumes (₹ crore, one leg) of: call money 14,431.90 (weighted average rate 5.63%), triparty repo 5,72,289.15 (5.53%), market repo 1,95,543.41 (5.61%) and repo in corporate bonds 7,492.65 (5.71%). Which statement is correct?

options.text: Triparty repo made up about 72.5% of the overnight volume, while call money made up under 2%
Call money was the largest segment, at about 72.5% of the overnight volume
Market repo made up about half of the overnight volume
The segment with the highest rate also had the highest volume

solution.concept: Composition of the overnight money market
solution.explanation: Total overnight volume = 14,431.90 + 5,72,289.15 + 1,95,543.41 + 7,492.65 = ₹7,89,757.11 crore. Triparty repo is 5,72,289.15 ÷ 7,89,757.11 ≈ 72.5%; call money is about 1.8%; market repo about 24.8%. The highest rate (5.71%, corporate bond repo) belongs to the smallest segment.
solution.why_others_wrong: Call money is the smallest overnight segment; market repo is about a quarter, not half; corporate bond repo has the highest rate but the smallest volume.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Triparty repo made up about 72.5% of the overnight volume, while call money made up under 2%

The cut-off yields were 5.8970% and 6.6485%. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The 91-day bill had the higher bid-cover ratio (about 2.70 against 2.56)
The 364-day bill had the higher bid-cover ratio (about 2.70 against 2.56) and the higher cut-off yield
Both bills had the same bid-cover ratio of about 2.6
The 364-day bill had the lower cut-off yield, as it was more heavily bid

solution.explanation: Bid-cover ratio = competitive bids received ÷ notified amount. 91-day: 20,465.33 ÷ 8,000 ≈ 2.56. 364-day: 18,875 ÷ 7,000 ≈ 2.70. The 364-day cut-off yield (6.6485%) was also higher than the 91-day yield (5.8970%), as is usual for the longer tenor.
solution.why_others_wrong: The ratios are swapped in the second option and not equal; the 364-day yield was higher, not lower.
solution.final_answer: Option B: The 364-day bill had the higher bid-cover ratio (about 2.70 against 2.56) and the higher cut-off yield

When it is genuine, clean enough for its denomination to be readily ascertained, and passes every fitness parameter
When it belongs to any series ever issued by RBI
